bet.text: Ship a simple robot before week 1 and protect driver practice: every hour spent inventing is an hour drivers do not get.

demand.text: The team says top-tier matches score 250 to 300 points and aimed to reach that line consistently rather than chase a higher peak, with a forgiving wide intake feeding a high-rate fixed shooter. A level 1 climb's 25 points was not worth fitting a climber before week 1.

auto.text: Preplanned Choreo trajectories that account for the robot's physical parameters.

cycle.text: One button deploys the intake and one shoots. Periodically the code senses by current whether there are 20 or more balls, then stages about 12 in the feeder for the next shot. Beyond the scoring zone a separate shot map feeds instead.

endgame.text: No climber; the team left it out.

fallback.text: If a hit makes the hopper ride over the intake, another collision lets it recover during the match.

gave_up.text: A climber, and turret and dual shooters.
Before the championship it dropped a hopper redesign, geometry tweaks and weight reduction because each risked a working robot.
Choreo paths are tuned to one configuration, so a mid-season rebuild forces a re-tune.
In weeks 1 and 2 the driver stayed more on the home half because the intake was fragile.

changed.text: The triple shooter and its three-channel hopper floor were replaced by a drum before the district championship.

The intake shaft bent at the first event, and the intake exploded at the district championship; it was rebuilt with plates that flex. The process page calls that the only mechanism change afterward; the interview also describes a slot that stiffened the hood.

outcome.text: 60-13-0 in official play; won the Archimedes division; pick 1 of the Archimedes alliance on Einstein; ranked 9 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 321.90, Archimedes).

facts.text: Uses the CTRE Swerve Tuner; switched to FOC control mid-season

functions.name: Intake

solves.text: Survive corner and wall hits at competition

functions.type: tube roller intake on flexing plates

facts.text: The tube flips over, so a hit does not mean removing the shaft
Compliant wheels, down from 2.25 in to make room for the tube
Two 0.25 in SRP plates stacked on each side flex like a leaf spring instead of fighting impact
The roller assembly detaches, so it survives plate swaps
The arm homes by a current spike at the hardstop
While deployed in hold mode, the heading locks to the direction of movement

cost.text: Four iterations through the district championship: polycarbonate plates did not last, the roller shaft kept taking hits, and the fourth version exploded

functions.name: Hopper walls

solves.text: Expand the hopper with the intake

functions.type: polycarbonate walls pushed out by the intake

facts.text: Material 1/8 in polycarbonate; the intake pushes the walls out as it deploys
A lower front part makes it ride over the intake less often after a hit

cost.text: The intake sometimes stuck on rivets, which were flipped around

solves.text: Funnel balls into the feeder and still reach the electronics

facts.text: Three flex-wheel rollers in front push fuel better; weight kept the team from making all of them live axles
Two screws release the floor so it pivots up for the electronics

cost.text: Each shooter rebuild forced a hopper redesign, because feed geometry has to match the shooter

functions.name: Feeder

solves.text: Empty the hopper faster than the first robot's single X44 could

functions.type: three feeder rollers on two motors

facts.text: Two Kraken X60 motors, one on each side, at a 12 to 30 ratio
Compression was lowered from the first design so balls move more easily

functions.name: Drum shooter

solves.text: An open fuel path with no settling step and a higher ceiling than three channels

functions.type: full-width drum with pivoting hood rollers

facts.text: Full-width roller diameter
Four Kraken X60 motors and two pivoting hood rollers
A jack shaft carries power to a brass flywheel on the other side, to stay inside the frame perimeter
A slot in the hood stops it vibrating left and right, which had spread shots
Early shooter pulleys (the page does not say on which version) chewed themselves up and were rebuilt with more infill and two 0.25 in square steel shafts inside

solves.text: Stage balls only when there are enough to be worth it

facts.text: Extra capacity from holding balls in the feeder, about
Hopper current is sensed periodically; above a threshold, 20 or more balls are in the hopper

functions.name: AutoAim

solves.text: Align to the hub with one button and little tuning

functions.type: interpolated shot map and two hub-facing cameras

facts.text: The shot map is measured and tuned by hand, not modeled
A first-shot compensation from data
Two OV2311 global-shutter cameras angled inward at the hub tags, on PhotonVision
Adapted from 6328 and the NINJAS, with iterative target shifting and gates on when to fire
Safeguards and filtering were added against electrical and dynamic edge cases

functions.name: Feeding map
functions.type: separate shot map outside the scoring zone

facts.text: Turns on by itself past the allowed scoring zone, so the driver does not switch modes

solves.text: Change mechanisms mid-season without rewriting the controls

facts.text: Subsystems publish state to one supervisor, so mechanism swaps did not need the controls rewired

decisions.because: weeks 1 and 2 were early and practice time mattered; the driver says it gave about two full weeks of practice, the binder more than three
decisions.instead_of: a turret or drum, which the team was about to over-scope

decisions.because: its indexer was too complex and there was no way to prototype, assemble and tune it before week 1; the team says scrapping it freed about three weeks
its ball rate ceiling was too low and funneling added a bottleneck
the drum had the higher ceiling: an open fuel path and no settling step
decisions.instead_of: the triple shooter, which had no logjams and was right for week 1

decisions.choice: Change only what the drum needed
decisions.because: the binder says it changed only what it had to, hopper hubs and floor wheels; the process page says each shooter rebuild forced a hopper redesign
25 points from a level 1 climb was not worth the cost of fitting one before week 1
it caught ball variation, release behavior and field conditions better than physics in the time available

decisions.choice: Only robustness work before the championship
decisions.because: optimization ideas each risked a working robot, and the intake was the proven failure point
decisions.instead_of: a hopper redesign, geometry tweaks and weight reduction

decisions.choice: Two cameras crossed inward on the hub
decisions.because: they give a good field of view and focus the processing on hub tags
